subject: Oceanography
title: Methane and Polar Warming
description: A short lesson to help you apply Methane and Polar Warming.

hook.text: Methane hydrates on the Arctic seafloor hold more carbon than all known fossil fuel reserves—locked in ice cages.

buildup.text: Gas hydrates form when methane is trapped in ice-like crystal structures under high pressure and low temperature.

discovery.text: Warming bottom water can destabilize hydrates—releasing methane, a greenhouse gas 80 times stronger than CO₂ short-term.

twist.text: Methane bubbles have been observed rising from the warming Arctic shelf—though their atmospheric impact is debated.

climax.text: A sudden large release—the 'clathrate gun' scenario—could trigger runaway warming, though most see gradual risk.

punchline.text: Frozen fuel on the seafloor—a sleeping giant we'd rather not wake.

quiz.question: What are methane hydrates?
options: Methane trapped in ice-like structures on the seafloor
